Gas is on track for the most expensive Thanksgiving ever recorded.

Regular averaged $3.82 a gallon on Nov. 15, against $3.08 a year earlier — and AAA's previous Thanksgiving Day record was $3.58, set in 2022. The national average has never been above $4 on Thanksgiving Day.

AAA expects 81.5 million Americans to travel at least 50 miles between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30, just under last year's 81.6 million and the first dip after three straight record years. Of those, 72.9 million are driving, down from 73.1 million.

My take: the table got cheaper this year and the drive didn't. For a lot of families the trip is now the expensive part of the holiday, not the meal.

Are you driving less this Thanksgiving — or just budgeting more for it?
